properties.name: Success is read from the authoritative object, never from a tool's local exit code
properties.statement:
When a command acts on something outside itself — a remote service, a subprocess, a pipeline, a build artifact — read the OUTCOME from the authoritative object, not from the wrapper's exit status. A tool reporting failure on its local half is not evidence the act failed, and a zero exit is not evidence it succeeded.

FOUR MEASURED INSTANCES, all on this project, all 2026-08-14 or earlier:

1. **`gh pr merge` — FIVE TIMES on 2026-08-14.** It printed `git: 'remote-https' is not a git command` and a fast-forward warning, which reads exactly like a failed merge. **The merge had already succeeded server-side every time**; what failed was gh's LOCAL post-merge sync. The authoritative read is `gh pr view <n> --json state,mergeCommit`. ⚠️ Retrying on the apparent failure is how a branch gets merged twice or force-pushed over.

2. **`fact:a-piped-gate-reports-the-pipes-exit-code-not-the-gates`** — `cargo test --workspace | grep | tail` was reported as passing. **A pipeline's exit code is its LAST command's**, so that zero belonged to `tail`. Caught only because 20 suites / 250 tests looked low against the real 103 / 1,138. Redirect the gate to a file and read `$?` from the gate itself.

3. **🔴 NEW 2026-08-14 — A GREEN TEST SUITE IS NOT EVIDENCE THE BINARY DOES THE THING.** Building `cap:nudge-absence-says-why`, all 19 unit tests passed while `target/debug/reflow2-mcp` was still the PREVIOUS build: **`cargo test --lib` compiles the library and its test harness, not the executable target.** A live call against that binary still returned the old answer. Only `cargo build -p reflow2-mcp` then re-running the live call showed the change. **The suite was authoritative about the library and silent about the artifact a user runs, and those are different objects.**

4. **🔴 NEW 2026-08-14 — A CORRECT SOURCE FILE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF WHAT IS SERVED.** Skills are embedded into the binary by `build.rs` at COMPILE TIME, so editing `getting-started/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` changes what is served only after a rebuild. `skill_lint` passing and the three trees being byte-identical say nothing about the running server. The authoritative read is asking the rebuilt binary: `get_skill` and check the body.

⭐ **WHAT 3 AND 4 ADD TO THE RULE, AND IT WIDENS THE DETECTOR IT OWES:** the first two instances are about EXIT CODES; these two are about BUILD ARTIFACTS. Same shape — the value you read is not the value you think you are reading — but a check that only scans for piped gates and CLI exit codes would miss both. **A detector for this rule has to cover "was the thing you measured the thing a user gets?" as well as "was the status you read the status of the thing you ran?"**

THE SHAPE ALL FOUR SHARE: **the misreading looks exactly like the answer you wanted.** That is why advice was not enough — AGENTS.md already tells agents to read results sceptically, and all four happened anyway.

ENFORCEMENT: **ENFORCED, on Anthony's word 2026-08-14** — asked whether breaking it should stop the build, he said stop the build. He is the first person to choose an enforcement value on this project deliberately; `dec:does-enforced-default-to-gate-blocking` records that reflow2's other four enforced rules acquired that state from a default nobody chose.

🛑 **WHAT THIS RULE OWES, STATED RATHER THAN QUIETLY SATISFIED.** An enforced rule raises `unverified_enforced_rule` at severity 0.6 until a PASSING Verification detects violations of it. **No check is attached, and none should be attached to close the finding** — `governance-proposal` is explicit that a passing check which tests nothing is a lie the graph cannot see. The finding stays open until a real detector exists.

✅ THE EXIT-CODE HALF IS CHECKABLE FROM THE REPO: a gate piped through `grep`/`tail`/`head` before its status is read, or a remote-acting CLI whose exit code is taken as the outcome — `tools/` and `.github/workflows/` are both in-repo and greppable. ⚠️ **THE BUILD-ARTIFACT HALF MAY NOT BE**, since "did you rebuild before you measured" leaves no trace in the repository. That asymmetry is worth knowing before somebody attaches a check that covers half the rule and reads as covering all of it.
